newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 9.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* SAFECO Corp is expected to announce a deal to acquire Lincoln National Corp's American States Financial Corp unit for $2.82 billion.
* Cablevision Systems Corp appears close to a deal to acquire a large portion of New York-area subscribers from Tele-Communications Inc for more than $1 billion.

* Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern Corp is looking to finance a $1.2 billion freight line that would put it in direct competition with Union Pacific Corp and Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp for the U.S. coal market.
* The unemployment rate dropped to 4.8 percent in May, the lowest level since November 1973.
* The United Auto Workers union is readying for job actions at three General Motors Corp plants.
* IBM is expected to unveil on Monday an upgrade to its line of microprocessor-based mainframe computers.
* Excel Communications Inc has agreed to acquire Telco Communications Group Inc for $1.08 billion.
* Cable and Wireless Plc has agreed to shed its 5.5 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd to state-owned China Telecom for $1.2 billion.
* The Dow Jones Industrials rose 130.49 to 7435.78 on Friday.
* The Treasury is expected to broaden its experiment with "inflation-indexed" notes through auctions of five-year notes in July and October.
* Xerox Corp agreed to pay $1.5 billion to buy Rank Group Plc's stake in their joint copier venture.
* Atlas Air Inc has agreed to buy 10 new 747-400 freighter jets from Boeing Co.

* Heard on the Street: By buying low and selling high, leveraged-buyout funds run by Thomas H. Lee, Blackstone Group and Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette have made fabulous profits for investors in recent years. But they now have a lot of imitators.

* Credit Markets: The Treasury will announce today that it plans to expand its experiment with "inflation-indexed" notes with an auction of five-year notes in July and another in October, Clinton administration officials said.
